source_ref: Reyes M, Vance-Chalcraft H (2022) 'Understanding undergraduate students' eHealth usage and views of the patient-provider relationship', PLOS ONE 17(4):e0266802, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0266802 (CC BY 4.0). Deposit: S3 File survey data (.s006, CSV) -- the file data/reyes_2022_eheals.py reads; S1 File survey questions (.s004, PDF); S3 Table per-item means (.s003, PDF). INSTRUMENT SOURCE for the wording: Norman CD, Skinner HA (2006) 'eHEALS: The eHealth Literacy Scale', J Med Internet Res 8(4):e27, doi:10.2196/jmir.8.4.e27 (CC BY 2.0, PMC1794004) -- Table 1 (the Q1..Q8 numbering) and Multimedia Appendix 1 (jmir_v8i4e27_app1.doc, sha256 1be20ad14af61daaf65d384ff495415dd553e6b554eea4dc140655d0fec0084a, the full administered form). All cached under .cache/reyes_2022_eheals/.
note: MAPPING CHAIN. data/reyes_2022_eheals.py renames the deposit's eight columns 'eHEALS question N from Norman CD, Skinner HA...' to eheals_N by explicit substring match (number-preserving rename; note the source has a typo 'eHEALS question 61' for question 6, which the script handles). The deposit publishes no eHEALS wording at all: the survey PDF (S1 File p.7) says only 'Items from Norman and Skinner (2006) were included here. See Table 1 in their original publication for the items', and S3 Table repeats that pointer. That sentence is what fixes the numbering, and it matters, because the instrument's own Multimedia Appendix 1 orders the same eight items differently (appendix items 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 = Table 1's Q3,Q4,Q1,Q2,Q5,Q6,Q7,Q8), so 'eHEALS question 1' is 'I know how to find helpful health resources on the Internet' (Table 1 Q1) and NOT the appendix's first scored item. Verified against data, not assumed: see verify_reyes_2022_eheals.R -- S3 Table's eight published means reproduce as 5 - mean(resp) for all eight items to within rounding (max deviation 0.0045 against a 2 dp half-width of 0.005; overall 2.7116 vs the published 2.71), and the only pair a 2 dp table could hide, Q3 2.76 vs Q4 2.75, is excluded by the swap counterfactual (0.0143). TEXT. item_text is transcribed from Multimedia Appendix 1, the instrument's own administered form, rather than from Table 1, which abbreviates two of them; the two differ only for eheals_2 (appendix 'I know how to use the Internet to answer my questions about health' vs Table 1 'I know how to use the Internet to answer my health questions') and eheals_7 (appendix 'I can tell high quality health resources from low quality health resources on the Internet' vs Table 1 'I can tell high quality from low quality health resources on the Internet'). The other six are word-for-word identical in both, which is itself a check on the pairing. instructions is the appendix's own preamble, verbatim; see public_note, it is interviewer-phrased and this study fielded online. OPTION TEXT is from the study's own materials, not the instrument: row 0 of the S3 File CSV is a Qualtrics codebook key row reading 'Key: 1 = Strongly agree, 2 = Agree, 3 = Neither agree nor disagree, 4 = Disagree, 5 = Strongly disagree', identical in all eight item columns. That is a data label and it REVERSES the instrument's own appendix coding (1 = Strongly Disagree ... 5 = Strongly Agree), so the anchors are shipped in the deposit's direction, not the instrument's. Two independent confirmations that the deposit key is the one the live integers follow: the affine fit above (published score = 5 - resp, i.e. agreement falls as resp rises), and the paper's own reading of its mean of 2.71 as 'students generally agreed'. Also note 'Neither agree nor disagree' (deposit) where the appendix prints 'Undecided'. RIGHTS. No restriction locatable to quote, and here there is more than silence: the rights holders themselves published the complete instrument, including the note that questions 3-10 constitute the scale, in a CC BY 2.0 JMIR article (PMC license-ref 'CC BY'). The commercial listing at eprovide.mapi-trust.org/instruments/ehealth-literacy-scale renders client-side and returned no text on fetch (3 KB, 'Website'), so no clause could be read there either way -- recorded because absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause. No row exists for eHEALS in instrument_rights_register.csv and none was written (a round may not write a ship-shaped row). LANGUAGE: administered in English (US undergraduates), so language and the _translated columns are omitted. correct_response is blank throughout; the eHEALS has no correct answer.
public_note: Neither this study's survey document nor its data file reproduces the eHEALS wording -- both point the reader to Table 1 of Norman & Skinner (2006) -- so the item text and instructions shipped here are the published instrument's own, which means the instructions retain the interviewer-administered phrasing 'tell me which response best reflects your opinion' even though this study fielded the scale online through Qualtrics

source_ref: Horvath et al. 2023 PLOS ONE 18(2):e0282000 Table 2 (RFQ-8 items, CC BY 4.0); cross-checked vs Zaal et al. 2023 PLOS ONE 18(6):e0287751 Table 2 and Kalaitzaki et al. 2024 PLOS ONE 19(2):e0298023 Table 1; response anchors and scoring key from the study's own SPSS deposit doi:10.7910/DVN/BMCC4C (CC0 1.0)
note: Administered in Polish; ships the canonical English RFQ-8 wording in the base fields as a translated_substitute, with the _translated columns empty. Recoverability was checked and the administered Polish is NOT in scope: the Harvard Dataverse deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/BMCC4C) holds a single file, the SPSS original of Wozniak-Prus_et_al_RFQ-8_study, whose variable labels for RFQ1..RFQ8 are all NULL and whose only value labels are the 1/7 endpoint anchors -- zero Polish item text anywhere in it -- and the paper (Wozniak-Prus, Gambin, Cudo & Sharp, 2022, J Pers Assess 104(6), doi:10.1080/00223891.2021.2014505) is closed access with no repository copy (OpenAlex oa_status=closed) and no supplementary files. The rights holder DID publish an official Polish form, RFQ_PL_8_items.doc, linked from ucl.ac.uk/psychoanalysis/research/reflective-functioning-questionnaire-rfq, but that page and its files are gone from the live UCL site (the page 301s to /brain-sciences/pals/psychoanalysis and the .doc soft-404s to the same landing page); it is not in the Wayback Machine either (404 at every timestamp tried). Off-source hunting for the Polish original is a later pass, not a blocker. ENGLISH SOURCE: transcribed from Horvath et al. 2023, PLOS ONE 18(2):e0282000, Table 2 (CC BY 4.0), which lists all eight RFQ-8 items in canonical order with item 7 annotated '(reversed)'; the '(reversed)' annotation is the authors' and was dropped. Cross-checked verbatim against Zaal et al. 2023, PLOS ONE 18(6):e0287751 Table 2 (which labels the same texts RFQ1..RFQ8) and against the RFQ-54 wording in Kalaitzaki et al. 2024, PLOS ONE 19(2):e0298023 Table 1 items 1/16/20/36/40/44/8/28. Two deviations from literal transcription, both deliberate: typographic apostrophes in the PDF were written as ASCII apostrophes, and the Kalaitzaki reproduction places commas after 'angry' and 'insecure' where Horvath does not -- Horvath's punctuation was kept because that table is the RFQ-8 form specifically. MAPPING: the .sav has no variable labels, so RFQ1..RFQ8 were tied to text by the instrument's own published item numbering and then checked against the data -- see verify_rfq_wozniakprus_2021.R, five predictions, all PASS. RESPONSE ANCHORS -- SOURCE OVERRIDE: the .sav labels 1='strongly disagree'/7='strongly agree' for RFQ1-RFQ7 but 1='strongly agree'/7='strongly disagree' for RFQ8. The RFQ8 label is an error in the source file and was overridden: the deposit's own RFQu8 column applies the identical ascending uncertainty recode (5,6,7 -> 1,2,3) that it applies to RFQu2/u4/u5/u6, reproducing every row exactly, and RFQ8 correlates +0.201..+0.354 with the other non-reversed uncertainty items and -0.203 with the reverse-keyed RFQ7. All eight items therefore ship 1=Strongly disagree ... 7=Strongly agree. Scale points 2-6 are left blank because the .sav labels only the endpoints; they were not padded with their own numbers. RIGHTS: no restriction found that blocks. The rights holder's page (UCL Psychoanalysis Unit, archived 2025-11-12 at web.archive.org/web/20251112174812/, retrieved sha256 of the archived HTML is not stable so the quotes are given in full) states under 'Availability': "The RFQ is freely available to download for research purposes. The measure is not yet suited for clinical purposes." The second sentence DISCLAIMS FITNESS and does not block (the LOT-R rule, 2026-09-08). The first states free availability and carries none of the six reserving terms -- no fee, no permission-required, no non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause, and no 'contact us for other uses' gate (the page's only contact line is scoped to translating the RFQ). It is softer than the hexaco.org clause, which reserved with 'but only for the purpose of non-profit academic research' plus a contact gate. This reads as ship-shaped, but the purpose phrase 'for research purposes' is close enough to the HEXACO shape that the judgement is ESCALATED rather than decided: per the 2026-09-10 rule no instrument_rights_register.csv row was written, and none should be until a human rules. Nothing was written to that file.
public_note: The RFQ-8 was administered to this Polish sample in Polish, but the study's deposit and its closed-access paper contain no Polish item wording and the rights holder's official Polish form is no longer distributed, so the item text shipped here is the canonical English RFQ-8 wording standing in for what respondents actually read. Item RFQ8 ships its stem but NO response-option labels, deliberately. The source SPSS file labels RFQ8's scale in the opposite direction to the other seven, and the processing script that built this table mapped on those labels, swapping only the two labelled endpoints (1 and 7) while leaving the unlabelled middle points 2-6 as they were. RFQ8's response values in this table are therefore not in a consistent order and no set of anchors describes them correctly, so none is given; RFQ8 should not be scored until the response data is reprocessed. The other seven items are unaffected and run 1 = Strongly disagree to 7 = Strongly agree, the direction the study's own derived scoring columns confirm. Only the two endpoints carry labels for any item, because the source labels only the endpoints.

source_ref: https://innovation.ox.ac.uk/outcome-measures/musculoskeletal-health-questionnaire-msk-hq/ (rights); PLOS S1 Appendix 10.1371/journal.pone.0308623.s001 (MSK-HQ-PT wording, not shipped); S2 Appendix .s002 (MSK-HQ-UK original, not shipped)
note: BLOCKED on instrument rights, not on access. The wording is fully recoverable: PLOS S1 Appendix (journal.pone.0308623.s001, .docx) prints the complete administered European-Portuguese MSK-HQ-PT -- 3 tables, items numbered 1-15 with their full five-point anchor sets ("Nada / Ligeiramente / Moderadamente / Muito / Muitissimo"; "Nunca / Raramente / Algumas vezes / Frequentemente / Sempre"; the 0-7 days physical-activity item) -- and S2 Appendix prints the original English MSK-HQ-UK, so an administered-language extraction with an English _translated twin was ready to build. Rights holder is Oxford University Innovation Ltd (MSK-HQ developed by Keele and Oxford, funded by Arthritis UK), and its own instrument page reserves rights on two independent grounds: written permission required for any change to content/order/formatting (no-derivatives + permission-required), and a click-to-licence portal with a Payment Info step (licence fee / permission-required). Under the 2026-09-05 irw#1945 reserve-a-right test that is a block. The PLOS article is CC BY 4.0, but a CC BY appendix reproducing a restricted instrument does not launder it (2026-09-08), and the Portuguese version is a derivative of the restricted English original, so the administered-language route does not avoid it. Note the appendix carries no OUI copyright line at all. The block does bite: the IRW item codes are msk1..msk14, which carry no wording, so withholding item text actually withholds the instrument (contrast irw#2101/#2123). Clause: "No other changes to the formatting, order or content of the MSK questions and responses, or the copyright message, should be made without the written permission of the Clinical Outcomes team at Oxford University Innovation. -- and the same page routes every user to "REQUEST A LICENCE" at the OUI "CLICK-TO-LICENCE PORTAL", whose steps are "Language Selection / Intended Use Confirmation / Organisation / Your Details / Payment Info / Terms"." Source: https://innovation.ox.ac.uk/outcome-measures/musculoskeletal-health-questionnaire-msk-hq/ sha256 4c95941c6ed03638c78ee5f10e63aed0ec5e76c290f921e4bc1e66c644ce22c7, fetched 2026-09-10; portal https://process.innovation.ox.ac.uk/clinical/p/arthritisuk-musculoskeletal-health-questionnaire-(msk-hq)/msk-hq-questionnaire/1 sha256 3eedd3bf9033293cf8d84e9fe893ab2a4d6d85aeb44f1c15e50227f65d9c5ea7. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict. Nothing about an unchanged retry changes it; only an OUI licence grant permitting IRW redistribution, or OUI relicensing the MSK-HQ openly, would flip it.
public_note: IRW does not offer item text for this table: the Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire (MSK-HQ) is licensed by Oxford University Innovation, whose terms require written permission for any change to the questionnaire's content or order and route all users through a paid click-to-licence portal.

source_ref: Open-Source Psychometrics Project RWAS deposit https://openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/RWAS.zip (RWAS/codebook.txt + data.csv, collected 2015); administered forms https://openpsychometrics.org/tests/RWAS/ , /tests/RWAS/1.php (RWA items, POST-only) and /tests/RWAS/2.php (TIPI + VCL); IRW script data/rightwing_authoritariansim.R; instruments: Altemeyer, B. (2006) The Authoritarians, University of Manitoba (RWA scale, ch.1); Gosling, Rentfrow & Swann (2003) JRP 37:504-528 (TIPI)
note: Three instruments in one table, all transcribed verbatim from the openpsychometrics.org administration participants actually completed: the RWAS item page (POST to /tests/RWAS/1.php, whose <select name="Q1">.."Q22"> fields carry both the statement text and the 1-9 option labels 'very strongly disagree'..'very strongly agree') and the follow-up survey page /tests/RWAS/2.php (TIPI1-TIPI10 traits with the 1-7 'Disagree strongly'..'Agree strongly' labels, and the VCL1-VCL16 checkbox words). A GET of 1.php returns 0 bytes -- the page only renders on the POST the landing form makes, which is why every Wayback snapshot of it is empty; the fetch was reproduced twice. RWA section_prompt is the 'Procedure' sentence from the landing page https://openpsychometrics.org/tests/RWAS/; TIPI section_prompt keeps both administered lines ('In the table below...' plus the 'I see myself as:' stem), which is one sentence more than sibling artistic_preferences shipped for the same TIPI block. VCL option_text 'unchecked'/'checked' is the deposit codebook's own wording ('A value of 1 is checked, 0 means unchecked'), not a label anyone read -- the source renders bare checkboxes; same convention as machivallianism_test_vcl. The administered RWA wording differs in small ways from Altemeyer's book text (item 5 'judgement' and a closing period; item 20 'one right way' where the book has 'ONE right way'); the administered form governs and nothing was normalised toward the book. instructions left blank: no text applies across all three sections. correct_response blank throughout -- VCL6/VCL9/VCL12 ('cuivocal','florted','verdid') are non-words used as a validity check, but the deposit publishes no key. MAPPING: data/rightwing_authoritariansim.R assigns item as row_number() over unique(item) after pivot_longer, i.e. a script-invented integer with no trace of the source column, so the script was re-run over RWAS.zip's data.csv rather than reasoned about: surviving column order is q1..q22, tipi1..tipi10, vcl1..vcl16 = items 1..48. Confirmed against server-side aggregates, all 300 item x resp cells equal (see verification row). RIGHTS: no quotable restriction on any of the three. Altemeyer distributes The Authoritarians (c) 2006 free from theauthoritarians.org (sha256 7888ff68ce6eee23447ca98761f923f32c124b0264afe766718de4f80816723d), prints the 22-item scale in chapter 1 and invites the reader to take it; no fee, no NC, ND or no-redistribution clause is stated there or anywhere on the site. Gosling's TIPI page states 'ANYONE CAN USE IT FOR ANY PURPOSE. NO NEED TO ASK ME FOR PERMISSION.' The VCL is openpsychometrics' own. The openpsychometrics test page carries the site's standard 'This test is provided for educational use only. It should not be used as psychological advice of any kind and comes without any guarantee of accuracy or fitness for any particular purpose' -- boilerplate on every test page there (verified on /tests/FTI/), and a fitness disclaimer about the online service rather than a reserved right, so it does not block; quoted here per the LOT-R rule. CAVEAT ON THE TABLE NAME: only items 1-22 are the RWA scale; 23-32 are the TIPI and 33-48 the vocabulary check-list, so the dictionary Description ('a survey that probes facist ideologies') describes 22 of 48 items.
